headlines: MIAMI LAKES BAKERY FAILS STATE INSPECTION OVER SANITATION VIOLATIONS
DIRTY UTENSILS TRIGGER FAILED INSPECTION AT MIAMI LAKES BAKERY
WHAT STATE INSPECTORS UNCOVERED INSIDE A POPULAR MIAMI LAKES BAKERY
draft.article:
A Miami Lakes bakery failed a state inspection on Thursday after officials uncovered multiple sanitation and food safety issues. Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services inspector Caridad Delgado cited Los Balkanes Bakery, located at 16241 NW 57th Ave., for dirty equipment and improper food handling.

Delgado documented food debris encrusted on knives, kitchen utensils air-drying without being sanitized, and tongs used for chicharrón and pastelitos unwashed for over four hours.

State officials also issued stop sales on cheese pastries and pan de bono kept between 85 and 87 degrees inside a non-temperature display. House-made yellow corn dough wrapped in a plastic shopping bag also received a stop sale.

headlines: HILTON TO OPEN 289-ROOM MIAMI BEACH HOTEL IN 2027
FIVE HISTORIC MIAMI BEACH BUILDINGS BECOMING ONE HILTON
HISTORIC MIAMI BEACH BLOCK REVIVED INTO NEW LUXURY RESORT
draft.article:
A major piece of local architectural history is getting a massive revitalization. The new Hilton Miami Beach is scheduled to open in early 2027 at 2000 Park Avenue in the Museum Historic District.

The 289-room destination connects and restores five historic structures dating from 1938 to 1953 that stood vacant for years after surviving a 2012 fire. The block-spanning project highlights Streamline Moderne and Miami Modern styles, anchored by Henry Hohauser's 1939 Collins Park Hotel.

Located near the Miami Beach Convention Center, the property will feature three pools, including two on rooftops, a signature coastal restaurant, and a rooftop bar.

headlines: GEORGE PINO FOUND NOT GUILTY IN DEADLY MIAMI-DADE BOAT CRASH
NOT GUILTY VERDICT IN FATAL 2022 BOAT CRASH
MIAMI JURY CLEARS GEORGE PINO IN TRAGIC CHANNEL CRASH
draft.article:
A Miami-Dade County jury has found South Florida real estate broker George Pino not guilty of vessel homicide and manslaughter. Jurors deliberated for under two hours on Monday evening before delivering the verdict in the emotional trial.

The charges stemmed from a September 4, 2022, Labor Day weekend crash in Miami-Dade's Cutter Bank channel. Pino, 55, was driving his 29-foot Robalo boat during his daughter's birthday celebration when the vessel struck a boat marker.

Seventeen-year-old Lucy Fernandez died from her injuries. Katy Puig suffered catastrophic injuries requiring constant care, and every other passenger was injured. State Attorney Katherine Fernandez Rundle stated her office accepted the verdict while acknowledging the tragedy's lasting toll on the community.

Our area traces its formal beginnings back to February 4, 1836, the date Dade County was officially created. The county received its name after Major Francis L. Dade as well as the Miami River.

The year 1836 was also defined by significant military operations. Fort Dallas was constructed in that same year and served as a military base during the Second Seminole War.

Together, the establishment of the county and the military presence at Fort Dallas shaped our earliest chapter in 1836.
